summary.text: Plain pork bacon is cured pork belly sold raw, so cook it before eating. The three main ways are the oven, a skillet and the microwave.

selection.text: Look for slices with long veins of lean pink meat and relatively little fat, and buy before any date on the package.

storage.text: Refrigerate raw bacon at 40°F or below and use it within 7 days, or freeze it.
For quality in the freezer, the FDA chart lists 1 month and the USDA bacon sheet 4 months; frozen food stays safe longer.
Bacon you cooked yourself keeps 4 to 5 days in the refrigerator, or 1 month frozen.
Shelf-stable cooked bacon goes in the refrigerator once opened.

preparation.text: To separate cold slices, slide a dull butter knife along the length between the strips.
You can cook bacon straight from frozen.

safety.text: Bacon is too thin to check with a thermometer reliably; cooked crisp, it should have reached a safe temperature. Cured bacon can stay pink even then.
Cook bacon completely in one go; never partly cook it to refrigerate and finish later.
Well-done or burned bacon carries more nitrosamines than less well-done bacon, and microwaved bacon has less than fried.
Thaw in the refrigerator, in cold water or in the microwave, never on the counter; cook right away after cold-water or microwave thawing.
Do not wash raw bacon; cooking destroys any bacteria on the surface.
Air fryer: Food Network Kitchen tested it and found it too smoky to recommend as a safe practice.

why.text: Hands-off and tidy: King Arthur puts baking at about 5 minutes of hands-on time, with little of the work of frying.

steps.text: Line the pan with foil if you will not keep the fat, lightly oil-spray both sides of a cooling rack, and set it in the pan.
Lay the strips across the width of the rack.
Move the bacon to a paper-towel-lined plate and pat off the excess grease.

tips.text: Cold-oven start: lay strips on a foil- or parchment-lined rimmed sheet without overlapping, put it in a cold oven, set 400°F and bake 25 to 35 minutes.
No rack: lay up to a pound on parchment, bake at 350°F about 25 minutes until it starts to shrink, separate overlapping pieces, then bake 5 to 15 minutes more.
To keep the fat, drain it into a heatproof jar; with parchment you can instead fold it up with the fat and throw it away.

doneness.text: Bake until it is as dark and crisp as you like.
Cooked crisp, bacon should have reached a safe temperature, even if it still looks pink.

why.text: Choose the skillet to watch and turn each strip to the crispness you want.

steps.text: Lay the strips without overlapping in a cold skillet; do not preheat it.
Cook over medium heat, which renders the fat evenly.
Turn the strips as needed until they reach the crispness you want, 8 to 12 minutes.

doneness.text: Cooked crisp, bacon should have reached a safe temperature.

why.text: Choose the microwave for a few slices with little mess; it also forms less nitrosamine than frying, though it crisps a little less.

steps.text: Put four sheets of paper towel on a microwave-safe plate that holds 4 to 6 slices without folding.
Lay the slices in a single layer without overlapping.
Cover with two more sheets so no bacon peeks out.
Microwave on high about 1 minute per slice, checking halfway because microwaves differ.
Leave it on the towels for a minute or so; it crisps as it cools.

tips.text: If it looks nearly done early, finish in 30-second bursts rather than the full time.

doneness.text: Cooked crisp, bacon should have reached a safe temperature.
